interface.signature: def minStepToReachTarget(KnightPos: list[int], TargetPos: list[int], N: int) -> int:

preconditions.expression: len(KnightPos) == 2 and len(TargetPos) == 2 and 1 <= N <= 1000 and all(1 <= pos <= N for pos in KnightPos + TargetPos)
preconditions.description: KnightPos and TargetPos are 1-based coordinates within an N×N chessboard (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000).

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value >= 0 and all(0 <= x < N and 0 <= y < N for x, y in [(KnightPos[0]-1, KnightPos[1]-1), (TargetPos[0]-1, TargetPos[1]-1)]))
postconditions.description: If the target is unreachable, return -1. Otherwise, return the minimum steps (0-based) from the 0-based KnightPos to 0-based TargetPos.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value >= 0 and return_value == min(steps for steps in range(N*N) if any(all(0 <= (KnightPos[0]-1 + dx) < N and 0 <= (KnightPos[1]-1 + dy) < N for dx, dy in [(2,1),(1,2),(-1,2),(-2,1),(-2,-1),(-1,-2),(1,-2),(2,-1)]) and any((KnightPos[0]-1 + dx) == (TargetPos[0]-1) and (KnightPos[1]-1 + dy) == (TargetPos[1]-1) for dx, dy in [(2,1),(1,2),(-1,2),(-2,1),(-2,-1),(-1,-2),(1,-2),(2,-1)]))))
postconditions.description: The returned steps are the minimum possible moves for a knight to reach the target from the initial position, or -1 if no path exists.
